annotation.title_clean: AI and cyber security: what you need to know
annotation.title_en: AI and cyber security: what you need to know
annotation.authors_or_issuer: National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC), United Kingdom
annotation.summary_en: UK NCSC guidance for non-technical managers and board members on cyber security risks and benefits of AI tools, especially generative AI and LLMs. It covers prompt injection and data poisoning, promotes secure-by-design, and gives questions leaders should ask about accountability and incident response.
key_provisions_or_claims: Security must be a core requirement throughout the AI system lifecycle (secure by design).
LLMs face novel vulnerabilities such as prompt injection and data poisoning.
AI developers, not end users, should bear responsibility for security outcomes.
Points to the Guidelines for Secure AI System Development co-developed with CISA and 17 other countries.
Provides questions for leaders on accountability, supply chain, and incident response for ML systems.
